# Ask Alexa+ to Explain News Headlines in Simple Terms Every Morning

Imagine starting your day with a quick, plain-English summary of the headlines, all delivered by your Alexa+ device without you lifting a finger. This guide will show you how to set up your smart assistant to give you a 30-second news roundup that's easy to understand and keeps you informed. By the end, you'll be able to get your daily news briefing tailored just for you.

## Before you start
-   An **Alexa+ smart assistant device** (like an Echo Dot or Echo Show) set up and connected to Wi-Fi.
-   The **Amazon Alexa app** installed on your smartphone or tablet.
-   An active **Amazon account**.
-   Roughly **5-7 minutes** of your time.

## Step 1 — Open the Alexa App
To begin, find and tap the **Amazon Alexa app** icon on your smartphone or tablet. This app acts like a control centre for your Alexa+ devices, letting you customise settings and add new features. When you open it, you'll usually see the home screen, which might display cards with suggestions or recent activity from your device.

**IF IT LOOKS DIFFERENT:** If you can't find the app, look for the official Amazon Alexa logo, which is a blue speech bubble with a white outline. Make sure you're connected to Wi-Fi so the app can communicate with your device.

You'll know it worked when the app's main screen, featuring various cards and a navigation bar at the bottom, appears on your device.

## Step 2 — Navigate to Skills & Games
Next, you need to find the "Skills & Games" section within the Alexa app. Look for the **"More"** tab, usually located in the bottom-right corner of the screen. Tapping this tab will open a menu with various options, letting you manage everything from your shopping lists to your device settings.

**IF IT LOOKS DIFFERENT:** On some versions of the app, or on older devices, you might see a "hamburger" menu icon (three horizontal lines) in the top-left corner instead, or a "Discover" tab at the bottom. Tap whatever looks like a main menu to reveal more options.

You'll know it worked when a new screen slides up or appears, presenting a list of categories and features, including "Skills & Games."

## Step 3 — Search for News Briefing Skills
Now it's time to find the news content you want. From the menu you just opened, tap on **"Skills & Games."** This section is like an app store for your Alexa+ device, where you can add new capabilities or "skills." Once inside, look for a search icon (often a magnifying glass) or a search bar at the top of the screen. Tap it, then type in keywords to find relevant news briefings.

**IF IT LOOKS DIFFERENT:** The search bar might be immediately visible upon entering "Skills & Games," without needing to tap a separate icon.

💬 Example: `news briefing` or `daily news` or `simple news`

You'll know it worked when the screen displays a list of various news providers and services, each offering an Alexa+ skill.

## Step 4 — Choose and Enable a News Skill
With the search results showing, scroll through to find a news skill that suits your preference for simple explanations. Look for well-known news organisations that typically offer concise summaries. Once you've found one, tap on its name to view its details. On the skill's page, you'll see information about what it does and user reviews. To add it to your Alexa+, tap the **"Enable to Use"** or **"Launch"** button.

**IF IT LOOKS DIFFERENT:** The button might also say "Activate Skill." Some skills might ask you to link your account with the news provider for premium features, but many basic news briefings are free and don't require this.

You'll know it worked when you see a confirmation message on the screen, like "Skill enabled" or "This skill is ready to use," indicating it's now linked to your Alexa+ account.

## Step 5 — Customise Your Flash Briefing Settings
After enabling a skill, it's a good idea to customise your Flash Briefing, which is Alexa+'s personalised daily news summary. Go back to the main menu (by tapping "More" again), then tap **"Settings."** Within the settings, scroll down and look for **"Flash Briefing."** Here, you can see all the news skills currently active in your briefing. You can reorder them to hear your favourite news first, or toggle others off if they're not quite what you're looking for. This is where you can truly ensure you're getting summaries from sources that focus on plain language.

**IF IT LOOKS DIFFERENT:** The "Flash Briefing" option might be listed under a broader "News" or "Audio" section within settings, depending on your app version.

You'll know it worked when you've organised your preferred news sources, and their names appear in the order you'd like to hear them during your daily briefing.

## Step 6 — Ask Alexa+ for Your News
Now that you've set everything up, it's time to hear your personalised news! Simply walk up to your Alexa+ device and use the wake word followed by the command for your Flash Briefing. Your smart assistant, a voice-activated digital helper, will then start playing concise summaries from the news skills you enabled in the previous steps.

**IF IT LOOKS DIFFERENT:** If your device has a screen, it might also display visual headlines or images accompanying the audio. If Alexa+ says it doesn't understand, try speaking a little clearer or closer to the device.

💬 Example: "Alexa+, what's my Flash Briefing?"

You'll know it worked when Alexa+ acknowledges your command and starts delivering your personalised news summary, playing the headlines and brief explanations from your chosen sources.

## Step 7 — Refine for Simpler Explanations
If the news briefings you're getting still feel a little too complex or detailed, you can refine your choices. Go back to the **"Skills & Games"** section (as in Step 3). This time, use more specific search terms like "simple news," "brief news," or "plain language news." Explore new skills that explicitly state they offer easy-to-understand summaries. If you find a better option, enable it (Step 4), and then go back to your "Flash Briefing" settings (Step 5) to disable the overly complex skill and ensure the new, simpler one is included.

**IF IT LOOKS DIFFERENT:** Some skills might offer different "modes" (e.g., brief vs. detailed) within their own settings, which you might find by tapping on the skill name in your Flash Briefing list and looking for options.

You'll know it worked when your morning briefing sounds clearer, less jargon-filled, and easier to follow, giving you the key information without getting bogged down.

## Common mistakes
-   **Not having the Alexa app ready:** Many customisation options for Alexa+ devices are managed through the mobile app, not directly on the device itself. If you're struggling, make sure the Alexa app is installed and linked to your Amazon account.
-   **Choosing overly complex news sources:** Not all news skills are created equal when it comes to simplicity. If your briefing is too detailed, go back to Step 7 and actively look for skills that highlight "brief," "simple," or "headline" summaries.
-   **Forgetting the specific command:** Alexa+ needs a clear command to start your news. If you just say "news," it might play a single news story or a longer broadcast. Use the exact phrase "What's my Flash Briefing?" to get your curated summary.

## What this means for you
-   **In everyday life:** You can stay informed about current events without needing to read long articles or watch lengthy news broadcasts, all while getting ready in the morning or having breakfast. It's a convenient, hands-free way to keep up.
-   **For your business or work:** Quickly grasp major headlines that might impact your industry or daily operations, without diverting precious time to in-depth research, giving you a quick overview to start your workday.
-   **If you're just getting started:** The easiest first move is to open the Alexa app and explore the "Skills & Games" section. Just looking around can help you discover other useful features for your smart assistant.

## Try it now
Take out your phone or tablet, open the Alexa app, and try enabling just one news skill, like your local public broadcaster's daily briefing. Then, simply ask your Alexa+ device, "Alexa+, what's my Flash Briefing?" and listen to your first personalised news update.
